data.jobspec:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Flux batch script converted from LSF

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# LSF resources:
#   -J RNAseq
#   -q rna
#   -R "select[mem>4] rusage[mem=4]"
#   -o logs/snakemake_%J.out
#   -e logs/snakemake_%J.err

#flux: --job-name=RNAseq

# Omitted LSF option: -q rna (queue)
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run in a different queue with different priority/limits, affecting wait time and performance.

# Omitted LSF option: -R "select[mem>4] rusage[mem=4]"
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted LSF options: -o/-e with %J token
# Flux jobid token expansion for output/error paths is not portable across Flux versions/sites.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames per run.

set -o nounset -o pipefail -o errexit -x

module load singularity/3.9.2

# LSF/DRMAA submission from Snakemake is not portable to Flux.
# Omitted: Snakemake --drmaa "$args"
# Performance implication: jobs will not be distributed as separate scheduler-managed tasks; instead they run under this single allocation,
# which can reduce throughput and increase walltime unless you configure a Flux-native Snakemake executor.

snakemake \
  --snakefile Snakefile \
  --configfile config.yaml \
  --jobs 12 \
  --latency-wait 60 \
  --rerun-incomplete \
  --use-singularity \
  --singularity-args "--bind /beevol/home/rbilab --bind /beevol/home/wellskri --bind /beevol/home/wellskri/packages/bin --bind /tmp:/tmp"

reasons: No compute resources are requested in the Flux resource section (no nodes, tasks, cores, or time limit). This will typically result in a default minimal allocation that is unlikely to match the workload needs.

The original LSF job enforced a memory requirement (`rusage[mem=4]` / `select[mem>4]`), but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory, this can lead to under-provisioning.

The workflow is configured to run up to 12 concurrent jobs (`--jobs 12`), but the Flux resource section does not request CPU capacity to support that concurrency (e.g., cores/tasks), risking severe oversubscription.
issues: Snakemake's LSF/DRMAA integration was removed; without a Flux-native executor profile, all work will run within the single allocation and may oversubscribe resources if not sized appropriately.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

#BSUB -J RNAseq
#BSUB -o logs/snakemake_%J.out
#BSUB -e logs/snakemake_%J.err
#BSUB -R "select[mem>4] rusage[mem=4] " 
#BSUB -q rna

set -o nounset -o pipefail -o errexit -x

# Load modules
# Use locally installed packages for Majiq
# module load fastqc/0.11.7
# module load samtools/1.12
# module load STAR/2.7.9a
# module load subread/1.6.2
# module load bbtools/38.86
module load singularity/3.9.2

# LSF arguments
args=' 
  -q rna 
  -o {log}.out 
  -e {log}.err 
  -J {params.job_name} 
  -R "{params.memory} span[hosts=1] " 
  -n {threads} ' 

# Run snakemake pipeline
snakemake \
    --drmaa "$args" \
    --snakefile Snakefile \
    --configfile config.yaml \
    --jobs 12 \
    --latency-wait 60 \
    --rerun-incomplete \
    --use-singularity \
    --singularity-args "--bind /beevol/home/rbilab --bind /beevol/home/wellskri --bind /beevol/home/wellskri/packages/bin --bind /tmp:/tmp"
